result.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning
result.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Code: https://github.com/tinaxu226/trust-boundary-benchmark (available upon acceptance)
result.summary: In receiver-directed federated learning, each site draws a trust boundary. For every source and model component it judges, on its own data, whether the transfer helps (admit), harms (reject) or cannot yet be told (abstain). We ask whether this boundary holds over hundreds of rounds. Our benchmark has a federation of thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle for every evaluated transfer, paired seeds, an attack protocol, fourteen methods over 600 rounds and Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500. The answer depends on which boundary is measured. Across 20 paired CPU seeds, a gate judging against a fixed reference better identified transfers useful relative to the site's starting model. Yet it admitted 29% of transfers harmful to the model the site now has. A gate judging against the current model admitted 2% of harmful transfers on that target in the CPU tier, but missed many transfers useful to the starting model. Two short propositions explain these distinct failures. We also evaluate a held out audit that leaves gate verdicts intact. After training, it decides whether each final model is deployed or the site falls back to local training, and reports admissions that have gone stale. With independent audit data its guarantees hold after any training history. At 600 rounds the audit deployed 65 to 72% of models, none with negative benefit on its target, and kept 98% of the gain. No stale report had the wrong sign in our runs. With 20,000 audit observations, a variance-adaptive bound found 99% of stale transfers that cost at least 0.01 in log loss. A common-target Qwen3 comparison on 60 selected transfers shows the same tension over 100 rounds. With 38% adversarial sites, FedFomo and CS-Gate were the only evaluated methods with positive mean gain in every honest group.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建了一个长程联邦学习基准，让各站点对每个来源与模型组件的迁移在原数据上判定「接受／拒绝／弃权」，比较固定参考与当前模型两种信任边界在数百轮内的失效模式，并评估一种不改变门控判决的留出审计机制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「弃权＋事后审计＋陈旧性检测」的目标设定可能为 LVR 提供启发：如何判定某次中间状态更新对当前模型是否仍有正贡献、何时停止或回退，可供核查其审计与陈旧判据能否迁移到 latent 推理状态的贡献分配与验证。
